Part 1 - The V60 Portion [43 Minutes Total]:
Click for all details

00:08 - 00:14 (6 mins) | Intro to Filtered Coffee: Question to guests: "Cual es un filtrado? What is a filtered coffee?" Explanation: It is a beverage made with coffee grounds where water flows through a porous material. A filtered coffee is a clean, lighter form of making coffee, offering a sharp contrast to a heavy espresso.

00:14 - 00:16 (2 mins) | Intro to Equipment: Introduce the tools: Kettle, Grinder, scale, filters, and drippers. Point out the variety: "Here you can see different kinds of drippers: Origami, V60, V70, Tornado, etc."

00:16 - 00:24 (8 mins) | Instructor Demonstration: Walk through the brewing process with everything pre-staged (grounds ready, water hot). Hand out the recipe cards to the guests so they can follow along visually.

00:24 - 00:26 (2 mins) | Talk About the Coffee: Briefly explain the origin, roast profile, and flavor notes of the specific coffee bean they are about to brew.

00:26 - 00:46 (20 mins) | Hands-On Exercise: Cue: "Everybody to your station: Follow my instructions please and use your recipe card."
Step 1: Warm up your water to 86°C (push the button on the kettle).
Step 2: Put your beans into the grinder (the grind size is already preset for you).
Step 3: Purge (rinse) your paper filter with hot water.
Step 4: Put your server on the scale and the dripper on top. Click the 'Tare' button to set the scale to zero. Put the grounds into the dripper.
Step 5: Weigh the coffee and make sure there are exactly 15 grams. Tare the scale to zero again.
Step 6: When the water hits 86°C, pour the bloom: 45 grams of water. Wait 1 minute.
Step 7: Before all the water leaves the dripper, pour your second round of water: bring the total up by 100g (scale reads 145g).
Step 8: Before that water completely leaves the dripper, make your final pour of 90g (final scale reading: 235g).

00:46 - 00:51 (5 mins) | Conclusion & Evaluation: Cue: "Try it!" Everyone tastes each other's brews. Discuss how to improve or why a specific cup came out tasting the way it did.

Part 2 - Barismo / Espresso Portion [45 Minutes Total]:

00:51 - 00:57 (6 mins) | Intro & Tools: Question to guests: "What can we make with an espresso machine?" Explanation: Beyond an espresso, we use it to create milk-based drinks like a cappuccino and a flat white. Introduce the tools: Espresso Machine, portafilter, Grinder, Scale, Filter Basket, WDT Tool, tamper, and milk Jug.

00:57 - 01:27 (30 mins) | Hands-On Espresso Steps & Milk Texturing: The Steps to Make an Espresso:
Put the portafilter on the scale and set the scale to 0.
Press the portafilter against the grinder trigger and dose exactly 18 grams.
Use the WDT tool to stir and evenly distribute the grounds.
Use the tamper to press straight down firmly and evenly.
Place your scale onto the machine base. Lock the portafilter into the group head, place your cup on the scale, and set it to 0.
Press the extraction button and start the timer on the scale simultaneously.
Next (The Finish): Stop the shot when it hits your recipe target weight (e.g., 36 grams of liquid espresso in roughly 25–30 seconds).

The Milk Step: Purge the steam wand, texture cold milk in your jug to a glossy microfoam texture, and pour it into the espresso using the correct ratios for a cappuccino or flat white.

01:27 - 01:36 (9 mins) | Drinks Practice & Tasting: Allow guests to pull their own shots, steam their milk, build their custom drinks at their stations, and drink them.
